details:
LUNARIS is an integrated space mission simulator built by Team TetraTech to bridge the gap between complex orbital physics and accessible lunar exploration. By combining official NASA datasets, real-time physics calculations, 360° interactive visualizations, and artificial intelligence, LUNARIS allows mission planners, researchers, and space enthusiasts to evaluate candidate landing zones anywhere on the Moon within seconds.

1. Flexible Mission Configuration & Side-by-Side Comparison

Users can easily tailor simulations to fit their exact operational needs. You can run instant, deep-dive analyses for a single spacecraft and location, compare different mission dates and vehicles, or configure two completely independent scenarios side-by-side to perform detailed engineering trade-off analyses. To get started, you simply select landing coordinates on an interactive 3D Moon globe or 2D map and define your mission timeline. The system then automatically loads verified hardware limits—such as battery capacity (Wh), solar array specs, and maximum slope tolerances—for historical missions like Apollo and Lunokhod as well as modern commercial landers.

2. Comprehensive Engineering Assessment & Telemetry Reports

Rather than leaving you with raw numbers alone, LUNARIS acts as an active decision-support tool. When terrain slopes, shadows, or energy limits create operational risks, the platform does not just throw a warning; it actively guides you by recommending safer alternative launch dates or flatter nearby landing zones. All critical mission metrics are brought together onto a single screen, including 30-day illumination timelines showing sunlight percentages and longest continuous night durations, regional relief maps, landing dispersion circles, and terrain slope distribution graphs.

3. Direct Inline Site Analysis & Regional Polar Scanning

You can explore the lunar surface seamlessly without ever losing your workflow context. Clicking any coordinate directly on the map triggers instant, inline physics calculations right on the spot, letting you toggle rapidly between solar illumination, Earth communication line-of-sight, and terrain slope layers. Additionally, a high-resolution grid scanning engine maps out the entire South Polar circle, generating detailed topographic visualizations to highlight the safest landing corridors.

4. Interactive Time Simulation & 360° Ground-Level Rendering

LUNARIS lets you experience landing sites from both orbital and surface perspectives. You can drop down to ground level at any chosen coordinate to inspect the true local horizon line, elevation obstruction angles from surrounding hills and crater rims, and overall surface roughness. At the same time, an interactive timeline slider lets you scrub through time across the high-resolution 3D lunar globe and terrain mesh to watch solar angles shift and crater shadows move in real time.

5. Scientific Data Infrastructure

Every calculation inside LUNARIS is anchored in official aerospace datasets. NASA JPL ephemeris kernels are processed locally to compute topocentric Sun and Earth azimuth and elevation vectors with millimetric precision for any chosen coordinate and timestamp. Alongside this, the engine scans surrounding topography using high-resolution NASA LOLA elevation matrices to calculate the exact angles at which mountains and crater walls block sunlight or disrupt Earth communications.

6. Bilingual AI Assistant & Adaptive Interface Modes

The platform is built to be intuitive for both aerospace engineers and newcomers. Powered by a custom natural language processing model developed from scratch, the interactive chat assistant lets you ask questions freely in English or Turkish to query mission parameters and get alternative date or spacecraft recommendations backed by real NASA data. Furthermore, a single click in the bottom-left settings panel lets you switch between Advanced Mode, which reveals full engineering telemetry and technical ratios, and Simple Mode, which offers clear, jargon-free summaries for accessible exploration.
